score_matrix.rationale: Patch applies, touches only the three allowed files, and uses Status: Solved with Resolved by: UBU-D0342, so schema and allowlist pass. It directly answers all five subquestions: Task-versus-packet ownership (§21.5.1), the full executor type list with Phase 1 limits (§21.5.3), authority/evidence/privacy/output/review/deadline/escalation fields (§21.5.2 table), self-reminder semantics without handoff (§21.5.3), and the Phase 1 dogfooding slice with acceptance fixtures (§21.5.4). The decision record is scoped as a data-model contract and explicitly defers General Contractor, Association, and marketplace semantics, which matches the question's current direction. Deductions are for unverifiable cross-references, the removal of the prior status vocabulary without visible reconciliation elsewhere, and a schema that is heavier and denser than 'minimum' suggests. No blocking fix is required; a human reviewer should confirm the referenced decisions and sections exist and that no other text depends on the removed packet statuses.
risks: Replaces the existing packet status vocabulary (proposed, offered, accepted, in_progress, delivered, reviewed, rejected, completed) with four preparation-only states and relocates execution state to the §25.1.2 assignment record; any other DESIGN.md or DECISIONS.md text that references the removed packet statuses would become inconsistent, and this cannot be verified from the prompt.

Relies on many cross-references (UBU-D0137, UBU-D0074, UBU-D0157, UBU-D0177, §2.11, §3.10, §9.3, §21.2, §21.4, §25.1.2, §25.1.3, §27.3) whose existence and meaning are not verifiable here; the validation notes confirm ID uniqueness but not that these referenced sections and decisions say what the proposal assumes.

The 'minimum' schema is fairly heavy: every table row is required on an admitted packet and the proposal introduces roughly fifteen new field names (execution_brief, schema_version, packet_version, expected_task_version, capability_grant_refs, originating_context_bundle_refs, route_decision_refs, execution_limits, idempotency_key, supersedes_packet_ref, etc.). This expands data-model surface in a question that is flagged as human-approval-required.
Introduces `security_level: low` as a classification label for un-compartmented content; if that label is not already part of the privacy vocabulary it adds a new term without defining it.

Dense prose with many nested rules (approval binding, revision invalidation, retirement semantics) makes auditing harder than a shorter contract would; some of this detail may belong in later implementation decisions rather than the MVP data-model answer.
